description: Ten documented NASA and USGS astronomical and Earth-observation images selected for distinct gallery slots. Satellite composites and radar images explicitly labeled.

images.title: Spacecraft views of the planets
images.summary: NASA/JPL combined observations from Mariner 10, Magellan, Galileo, Viking and Voyager into a Solar System portrait. This is an edited montage, not one camera exposure; planet sizes are not consistently to scale.
images.alt: Montage of planets including Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and the Moon against black space.
images.caption: The Solar System as observed by multiple spacecraft, assembled in a NASA/JPL montage; the inner and outer groups use different scales.
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: Composite of archival NASA planetary images; relative planetary sizes are not uniformly to scale. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Venus's radar-mapped surface
images.summary: NASA's Magellan spacecraft mapped Venus beneath its opaque clouds using radar. Radar observations were projected onto a simulated globe centered at 180 degrees east longitude.
images.alt: Grayscale hemisphere of Venus showing radar texture, surface structures and a coordinate grid against black space.
images.caption: Venus's solid surface is hidden from conventional visible-light cameras by thick clouds, so radar mapping was used here; this is not a natural-color photograph.
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: Magellan radar mosaics mapped to a simulated globe, with data gaps filled by other radar observations or neutral tone. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Earth as a global satellite mosaic
images.summary: A hemisphere of Earth centered on Africa in NASA's Blue Marble Next Generation product, assembled from observations collected across time, not a single photograph.
images.alt: Full circular view of Earth centered on Africa with the Sahara, tropical forests and oceans visible.
images.caption: An Earth hemisphere from the Blue Marble Next Generation dataset; the image combines remote-sensing observations rather than capturing one instant.
images.credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Reto Stöckli and Robert Simmon
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation multitemporal composite, March 2005 view of Africa. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Victoria Falls and the Zambezi Gorge
images.summary: From the International Space Station, the Zambezi River turns sharply through successive basalt gorges near the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe.
images.alt: Rust-brown terrain crossed by the blue-gray Zambezi River and a jagged series of narrow gorges.
images.caption: A specific African landscape rather than a representation of the whole continent: the river erosion and faults that shape Victoria Falls.
images.credit: NASA / ISS astronaut Edward Lu / Johnson Space Center
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: ISS astronaut photograph; NASA annotation/crop may be visible in the supplied original. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Mount Everest and the Himalayan glaciers
images.summary: The Earth Observing-1 Advanced Land Imager photographed a region of the Himalaya centered on Mount Everest, illustrating Asia's immense tectonically uplifted mountain landscape.
images.alt: High rocky ridges and white Himalayan glaciers with deep branching valleys in a satellite image.
images.caption: Satellite view of Everest and the surrounding Himalaya; one example of Asian geography, not an overview of every Asian region.
images.credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Jesse Allen and Robert Simmon / EO-1 ALI
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: NASA Earth Observatory natural-color satellite mosaic or enhanced scene, source processing retained. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Amazon River bends in sunlight
images.summary: Sunlight reflects from the meandering Amazon River in a 2017 ISS astronaut photograph, revealing channels and surrounding South American forest.
images.alt: Bright silver river bends and channels meandering through a dark green forest landscape seen from orbit.
images.caption: The Amazon River in sunglint, photographed from orbit on 9 August 2017; NASA cropped, adjusted contrast and removed lens artifacts.
images.credit: NASA / Expedition 52 crew / ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: NASA ISS image cropped, contrast enhanced and lens artifacts removed by NASA. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Three Great Barrier Reef islands from orbit
images.summary: An ISS astronaut documented interlocking reefs, shallow turquoise lagoons, and dark channels off Queensland, Australia.
images.alt: Brilliant turquoise coral reef lagoons and shallow islands in dark blue tropical water.
images.caption: Three Great Barrier Reef reefs near the Whitsunday Islands, Australia, photographed on 12 October 2015.
images.credit: NASA / Expedition 45 crew / ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: NASA ISS photograph cropped and enhanced to improve contrast; lens artifacts removed. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Kong Oscar Glacier and ice mélange
images.summary: An Earth Observing-1 natural-color view shows a heavily crevassed glacier terminus and icebergs in northwestern Greenland.
images.alt: Bright white glacier with broken crevasses and scattered icebergs at the edge of dark rocky Greenland land.
images.caption: Ice from Kong Oscar Glacier drains toward Davis Strait. The image was observed on 14 May 2010.
images.credit: NASA Earth Observatory / Jesse Allen and Robert Simmon / EO-1 ALI
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: NASA natural-color Earth-observation image; no additional false-color rendering introduced here. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Dunes in Namibia's Namib Desert
images.summary: Landsat 7 captured repeating dunes and salt-plain terrain in Namib-Naukluft National Park in 2000. The orange and cyan appearance is a false-color composite.
images.alt: Intricate parallel orange sand dunes next to blue-gray ground and mineral flats.
images.caption: Landsat false-color composite of the Namib Desert, using near-infrared, green and blue bands; these are not natural visible-light colors.
images.credit: USGS EROS Data Center / NASA / Landsat 7 ETM+
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
images.processing: NASA/USGS Landsat false-color composite sharpened with the panchromatic band. NASA-supplied observational image; downsampled to at most 1800 pixels on each axis and re-encoded as quality-87 JPEG for the development archive; linked source retains the higher-resolution original.

images.title: Amazon rainforest and convective clouds
images.summary: Small cumulus clouds form over the forested Amazon Basin in an Aqua MODIS satellite scene, showing the connection between tropical vegetation, heat and moisture.
images.alt: Dark green Amazon forest covered by many tiny white popcorn-like cumulus clouds, with clearer ribbons over rivers.
images.caption: On 19 August 2009, NASA's Aqua satellite observed small cumulus clouds forming over the Amazon rainforest, likely aided by transpiration and afternoon convection.
images.credit: NASA / Jeff Schmaltz / MODIS Rapid Response Team, NASA GSFC
images.rights: NASA / US-government mission media; reuse subject to NASA Media Usage Guidelines and any third-party credit notices; verify independently before external flight selection.
